abstract: Platelet orientation offers a processing route for improving thermal transport in compliant polymer composites. Here, we examined whether vertical alignment of boron nitride platelets increases through-plane thermal conductivity in silicone films without a major loss of compliance. Vertically oriented and randomly dispersed films were prepared at the same filler fraction of 20 vol% using identical silicone formulations and curing conditions. Cross-sectional microscopy was used to assess orientation. At 25 °C, through-plane thermal conductivity was 1.8 ± 0.2 W m−1 K−1 for aligned films and 0.9 ± 0.1 W m−1 K−1 for random films, whereas tensile moduli were 2.4 ± 0.3 and 2.2 ± 0.2 MPa, respectively. Values are means ± sample standard deviations from five independently prepared films per group; no hypothesis tests were performed. Aligned films retained 92% of their initial conductivity after 500 bending cycles at a 5 mm radius. These results support improved measured conductivity with a modest increase in mean modulus under the tested conditions. Interfacial resistance, the underlying mechanism, and device-level thermal performance remain unresolved.
discussion: Prolonged heating at 110 °C altered the extractability and mechanical response of the disulfide-containing polyester network. Increasing the treatment duration from 15 to 60 min raised the THF sol fraction from 8% to 19% and lowered the storage modulus at 1 Hz and 25 °C from 6.0 to 3.8 MPa. These changes are consistent with network rearrangement and/or chain scission, but do not uniquely identify either process. The reported values are means from three separately prepared specimens per condition; without error estimates or statistical tests, their variability cannot be assessed. The approximately unchanged DSC glass-transition temperature of 42 °C indicates no resolved shift under these measurement conditions. Likewise, the absence of a resolvable shift in the ester carbonyl band does not exclude low levels of ester cleavage. The broader low-molar-mass shoulder observed by SEC after 60 min provides additional evidence of changes in the soluble material, although polystyrene calibration and exclusion of the insoluble network limit its interpretation. Attribution to disulfide chemistry also remains uncertain without an ester-only control. An otherwise matched ester-only network and end-group analysis would help distinguish the proposed processes. Although these observations motivate reprocessing studies, they do not establish recyclability, performance over repeated reprocessing cycles, or resistance to long-term creep.
results: The fabricated 10-bit SAR ADC was characterized at room temperature with a 1.0 V supply and a sampling rate of 20 MS/s. Five dies were measured; the results reported here are from one representative die and are not averages across the five dies. With a 1.1 MHz sinusoidal input, the measured signal-to-noise-and-distortion ratio (SNDR) was 57.2 dB, and the spurious-free dynamic range (SFDR) was 69.5 dB. At an input frequency of 9.7 MHz, the SNDR decreased to 54.8 dB, showing input-frequency dependence under the tested conditions. Peak differential nonlinearity was +0.45/−0.38 LSB, and peak integral nonlinearity was +0.72/−0.66 LSB. The ADC core consumed 0.62 mW, including the comparator, DAC switching, and SAR logic. This power accounting excludes the external reference driver and clock generator, and power was not swept across temperature. Fabricated in a 65 nm CMOS process, the active core occupied 0.018 mm², excluding pads. These measurements characterize the converter within the stated operating and accounting boundaries; they do not establish an advantage over prior work because no harmonized comparison was performed.
